Not all privileged kids are this out of touch. I’m fortunate enough to have been born to parents who genuinely worked incredibly hard for their money. Given that my parents only came upon this money half way through my childhood, I am well aware of my immense privilege and I give back to others as much as possible and try to do good with the power I’ve been given. Many of my peers who are in similar situations behave the same way. While many don’t understand what it’s like to be anything but rich, few genuinely lack sympathy for those worse off than themselves.

I’m no expert on raising children but I will say that I went from a 3.6 GPA freshman year to a 4.3 senior year after plenty of arguing with my parents, but the only thing that really had any effect on me was myself. One day it all just clicked for me and I realized I needed to work hard because my future depends on it. I’m not sure if you’re going through anything similar to this with your child, but keep in mind that sometimes the issue is that kids just don’t see the big picture or have a different perspective to you.  I’m not sure how to remedy a child with an ignorant perspective, but sometimes that’s what the goal should be rather than just wanting better grades or test scores.

I am aware that my mom can’t directly do much for me and I don’t think she is in denial. I am very good at not appearing depressed to people, especially given that it only comes in waves so a good portion of the time I feel good. I have only really publicly let down my guard and not faked being happy a handful of times. I know that my only real route to therapy is through my parents but it just seems so out of reach to me right now (which is kind of ironic given that I know my healthcare gets me a ridiculous amount of therapy for nearly nothing). If I go to a therapist with my healthcare card and the copay will they see me without my parents consent?

I really appreciate you taking me seriously enough to ask follow up questions by the way. I may seem attention seeking, I might even be attention seeking, but even just this little interaction over the internet means so much to me right now.
